title: Nonviolence
hook: a pope's peace message names active nonviolence as a way of life and of politics

segments.voice: Yesterday, the universal destination of goods: what you own is really yours, and the earth's goods are still meant for everyone. Your line was meant for all. What did you share? Day one thousand three hundred twenty-two.

A kitchen, late at night, two people mid-argument. One voice rises. The other has a choice: rise to meet it, go cold and silent, or try something harder. Paul, writing to the Christians in Rome, names that harder thing in a single line, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be not overcome by evil: but overcome evil by good." Not run from it. Not match it. Overcome it, with its opposite. Pope Francis wrote a message for the Church's World Day of Peace and put one word in its title, a word he carries from kitchens like that one all the way into politics. Today, nonviolence.
screen: `A KITCHEN, A RAISED VOICE.` → `OVERCOME EVIL BY GOOD.` → `A POPE'S PEACE MESSAGE.`

segments.voice: First, where Francis starts. His message goes back to the Sermon on the Mount. Jesus says to love your enemies, and in the Douay-Rheims, "do good to them that hate you." Francis reads that as a whole way of living, and he says it plainly: to be a true follower of Jesus today includes embracing his teaching about nonviolence. Second, the word that matters most in the carry: active. Francis is clear that nonviolence isn't giving up, or looking away, or letting a bully win. It's a choice to resist evil without copying it. He points to people who did exactly that and changed things, and among them he names Mother Teresa, and Martin Luther King. Nonviolence, in this message, takes courage and planning and nerve. It can stand in a street. Third, where it begins. Not first at a border or a parliament. Francis says it starts at home, in families, where people learn to argue without wounding and to forgive without pretending nothing happened. A kitchen table is a peace table too. Fourth, an honest note. The Catechism still keeps a place for legitimate defense, and Catholic teaching also thinks hard about when force can be just. Francis doesn't erase that. He asks that nonviolence become the first instinct and the normal style, in private life and in politics, with force a last and sorrowful exception. Two strands, held in one Church. Up close, it looks small: an angry reply left unsent, a voice lowered, standing beside someone instead of against them.
screen: `LOVE YOUR ENEMIES, DO THEM GOOD.` · `ACTIVE, NOT PASSIVE.` · `IT STARTS AT HOME.` · `DEFENSE STILL HAS A PLACE.` · then, large: `OVERCOME EVIL BY GOOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: respond to one conflict gently. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one conflict you're in right now, big or small. A coworker, a sibling, a neighbor, a thread online. Notice what you're holding ready: the sharp line you've been rehearsing, the silence meant to punish. Now, without giving up what's true, find the gentler move. A question instead of a verdict. A calmer sentence. Hold it, and breathe with it. If you pray, you can bring that person before God by name. The bell holds the time.
Nonviolence. Resisting evil without copying it: in Francis's message, a style for life at home and for politics, rooted in the Sermon on the Mount. Today's word.
Your line: active nonviolence. Today, when one conflict heats up, keep the truth and answer with good: one gentler reply, on purpose. Day one thousand three hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for peace at Mass and on the Church's World Day of Peace, and some Catholic groups train in nonviolent action; parish and family life is where the Church asks it to begin.

myth: in Francis's message, nonviolence means doing nothing
he calls it active: resisting evil without copying it, which takes courage.
the message roots nonviolence in Jesus' own teaching
it goes back to the Sermon on the Mount: love your enemies, do good to them that hate you.
the Catechism has no place for self-defense
it keeps a place for legitimate defense; Francis asks that nonviolence be the first instinct.

fork.setup: a coworker mocks you in a meeting, in front of everyone. what fits the active nonviolence of Francis's message?
options: stay calm, name what happened, and talk to them after.
say nothing, ever, and let it go on.
fork.reveal: active nonviolence is neither revenge nor looking away. it resists the wrong without copying it: overcome evil by good.

trapdoor: what you thought: nonviolence means staying out of trouble.
what it means: resisting evil actively, without using its weapons, starting at home.
what a scholar hears: a peace message that reads the Sermon on the Mount as a style of politics, held beside the Catechism's teaching on legitimate defense.

notes: The index hook names the year (2017); the voice states no year under the claims rule. Index hook kept in meta; the script's hook line reworded without the date.
